Business.description: What the major business and general-news outlets are leading with.
Business.overview: Coverage across major business and general-news outlets remains dominated by the fallout from this week's Democratic midterm sweep, especially its shock to AI and tech stocks and the scramble by hyperscalers to secure power and goodwill amid a data-center backlash. Secondary threads include new Democratic-led congressional investigations into Trump-linked businesses and crypto, a Houthi missile strike on Riyadh's financial district, and signs of strain in white-collar hiring and consumer spending heading into the holidays.

stories.headline: AI and data-center stocks whipsaw as investors digest midterm fallout
stories.summary: A historic Democratic sweep in the midterms triggered a trillion-dollar rout in AI and chip stocks over fears of tougher data-center regulation, before shares partially rebounded; Fortune and Forbes reported Dan Ives now expects AI capex growth to peak next year and that up to 20% of planned U.S. data centers could face long regulatory delays.

stories.headline: Anthropic strikes $3.4bn deal for gas-fired power at data centers
stories.summary: The AI lab is bypassing traditional suppliers, buying commitments for 1.7 gigawatts of heavy-duty generators to secure scarce power equipment as data-center energy demand surges amid political backlash over electricity costs.

stories.headline: Apple saves $2.7bn in taxes by booking profits in Singapore
stories.summary: New disclosures show Singapore has overtaken Ireland as Apple's biggest tax shelter for iPhone profits, according to the FT.

stories.headline: Democrats vow to impeach Trump officials and probe GOP donors, including crypto ties
stories.summary: Incoming Democratic lawmakers are targeting Pete Hegseth, Elon Musk and Venezuelan oil deals for congressional probes, while the FT separately reports the crypto industry bracing for investigations into the Trump family's ties after the midterm sweep.

stories.headline: Houthi strike hits Saudi Aramco tower in Riyadh's financial district
stories.summary: A Houthi attack damaged a landmark tower in Riyadh's financial hub, disrupting plans for normalcy about a month after earlier deadly strikes on the capital, with WSJ noting officials acknowledged damage to the building.

stories.headline: Talent wars are breaking the traditional law-firm model
stories.summary: A record year of partner turnover helped bring down Weil Gotshal and is pushing similar elite firms to restructure, as separately NYT reports AI law firm Crosby bought malpractice insurance for its AI agents amid gaps in insurer coverage of AI risk.

stories.headline: AI debt jitters grow as ING seeks buyers for $500 million in data-center loans
stories.summary: ING is auctioning roughly $500 million across a dozen data-center loans, including debt tied to a New Mexico Stargate site, as banks try to offload AI infrastructure credit risk amid growing political scrutiny of construction.

stories.headline: White-collar hiring jumps in October, complicating the AI-jobs narrative
stories.summary: A sector often used as a bellwether for white-collar employment added 70,000 jobs despite fears that AI is displacing such roles, though one economist called the data a "head fake," while Axios separately reported employers are hiring faster than economists expected even as layoffs stay low.

Business.gaps: No recent coverage found for Puck or Business Insider (the latter blocks web search and had no feed items provided); The Economist, Politico, NYT, FT, BBC and WSJ were represented only through the provided feed items plus limited corroborating search results.

US politics.overview: Coverage across these outlets remains dominated by the fallout from Tuesday's historic Democratic midterm sweep: Trump's reshuffling of his White House team (elevating Stephen Miller to chief of staff), an imminent House vote to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, a GOP reckoning over what went wrong, and Democrats consolidating new power in Congress and in statehouses nationwide.

stories.headline: Trump replaces Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller as chief of staff
stories.summary: Trump elevated hardline adviser Stephen Miller to chief of staff after blaming Wiles for the party's midterm losses, trading a moderating force for one of his most maximalist aides as Democrats prepare to take control of Congress.

stories.headline: House poised to impeach Hegseth as GOP defections mount
stories.summary: House Republican leaders are bracing for enough GOP defections to impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth this week, as Rep. Thomas Massie forces a floor vote over the secretary's conduct of the Iran war and lawmakers who lost reelection have little left to lose politically.

stories.headline: Democratic wave reshapes state power, flips a dozen legislative chambers
stories.summary: Democrats picked up more than 500 state legislative seats and flipped at least 12 chambers, giving the party its most legislative trifectas since 1984 and reviving debates over Medicaid expansion in holdout states.

stories.headline: Schumer projects confidence on reelection as majority leader, but faces grumbling from newcomers
stories.summary: Schumer predicted he'll be reelected majority leader of an enlarged 54-56 seat Senate Democratic caucus, even as some incoming senators-elect, including Maine's Troy Jackson and Minnesota's Peggy Flanagan, have said they want new leadership.

stories.headline: GOP governors and insiders begin post-midterm reckoning
stories.summary: Oklahoma Gov. Kevin Stitt blamed a lack of "civility" from Trump for the GOP's historic defeat, while Politico reports Miller's promotion is deepening fears inside the party that there will be no broader reckoning.

stories.headline: Democratic statehouse wins put Medicaid expansion back in play
stories.summary: In a handful of holdout states, Democrats are poised to use their new statehouse dominance to push Medicaid expansion under the Affordable Care Act, even as four Democratic state attorneys general separately sue over Trump's new Medicaid work requirements.

stories.headline: Democrats plot to end Iran war once they control Congress
stories.summary: Senate Democrats, buoyed by the midterm wave, are preparing to try to grind Trump's war with Iran to a halt next year, with some Republican support, as WSJ reports Trump's own advisers are split over whether to escalate or end the conflict.

stories.headline: Sotomayor says she hopes Supreme Court will overturn presidential immunity ruling
stories.summary: Justice Sonia Sotomayor said there are several decisions she dissented from, including the presidential immunity ruling, that she hopes the Court will eventually overturn.

US politics.gaps: NOTUS and Cook Political Report had no distinct recent stories surfaced in search beyond older midterm forecasting roundups already reported elsewhere; NYT, WSJ, and The Guardian block web search so only their feed items (mostly international/markets) were available and were largely outside the US politics scope.

Tech & AI.overview: Coverage over the past 48 hours is dominated by Anthropic's rocky path to an IPO and its massive infrastructure spending, broader fallout from the US midterms hitting AI/data-center stocks, and a cluster of security incidents (Chainalysis breach, alleged Chinese espionage against Nvidia's CEO) alongside AI copyright litigation against Suno. Enterprise-AI trade press (VentureBeat, The Decoder) is also tracking new model releases and data on how reliably AI agents actually work.

stories.headline: Anthropic pushes ahead with IPO at a lower valuation as tech stocks slide
stories.summary: Anthropic is proceeding with a pre-Thanksgiving IPO at a valuation of roughly $1.25-1.75 trillion, well below the previously hoped-for $2 trillion, as investors balk amid a broader tech selloff; Anthropic itself confirmed it has now filed its S-1 with the SEC for the offering.

stories.headline: Anthropic strikes $3.4bn deal for gas-fired power to feed data centers
stories.summary: Anthropic has reportedly committed to buy 1.7GW of gas-fired generators from equipment supplier OnePWR for $3.4 billion, described as the largest such purchase by any AI lab as it bypasses traditional power suppliers to secure scarce equipment.

stories.headline: Midterm 'blue wave' and local data-center backlash rattle the AI trade
stories.summary: A wave of Democratic midterm wins and a near-sweep of local ballot measures against data centers has intensified investor anxiety about AI stocks, with systematic trading amplifying the losses; TechCrunch and MIT Technology Review separately report the same backlash is putting Texas's AI data-center boom and Musk-linked projects at risk.

stories.headline: AI companies have already sold $300bn+ in stock this year, with $100bn more to come
stories.summary: Excluding Anthropic's IPO, AI companies have sold or priced more than $300 billion in stock in 2026 with roughly $100 billion more expected, raising questions about how much the market can keep absorbing.

stories.headline: US intelligence memo says Chinese executive was recruited to spy on Nvidia's CEO
stories.summary: A memo circulating among US officials reportedly alleges that China's Ministry of State Security recruited a female tech executive at Megaspeed to spy on Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang.

stories.headline: Chainalysis says hackers stole credentials and tokens for all of its customers
stories.summary: Blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed what it called a 'multifront cyberattack' involving AI agents and an on-path data theft that compromised credentials and tokens for its entire customer base.

stories.headline: Elvis and Eminem rights holders sue Suno over AI music cloning
stories.summary: Rights holders for Elvis Presley's catalog and the publisher behind some of Eminem's biggest records have filed new lawsuits against AI music generator Suno, adding to its mounting legal troubles.

stories.headline: Apple's Ternus pushes for more urgency on AI, wants Siri to go beyond tweaks
stories.summary: Sources tell Bloomberg that Apple hardware chief John Ternus is pressing software chief Craig Federighi to move Apple's AI efforts beyond incremental Siri fixes toward agentic and other advanced capabilities.

Tech & AI.gaps: The Verge, Wired, Ars Technica, NYT, WSJ, FT, The Economist, and The Guardian block direct web search, so coverage from those outlets is limited to the feed items supplied; no distinct recent items were found for Platformer, IEEE Spectrum, Rest of World, or Google DeepMind beyond what's reflected via Techmeme/other outlets.

Energy.overview: Coverage across energy and climate outlets is dominated by the fallout from this week's U.S. midterm elections, with Heatmap, Canary Media and Utility Dive all examining how Democratic wins will reshape clean energy, utility and permitting policy heading into 2027. Secondary threads include the run-up to COP31 in Turkey, big AI-driven power deals, and a string of utility financial and regulatory moves (Revolution Wind's completion, DTE's asset sale, and a new Trump order on foreign grid equipment).

stories.headline: Midterm 'blue wave' upends US energy and climate politics
stories.summary: Heatmap reports that Democrats' sweeping midterm victories halt what it calls Trump's 'energy revolution,' but the new class of Democrats ran on moderate, all-of-the-above energy platforms rather than aggressive decarbonization, with electricity affordability the dominant theme. Canary Media and Utility Dive both frame the same results as a turning point for utility regulation and clean-energy policy at the state level.

stories.headline: Rhodium Group: permitting bill likely to cut emissions even in worst case
stories.summary: Heatmap reports on new Rhodium Group modeling finding that the bipartisan permitting reform bill (BAAJA) would likely trim U.S. emissions and lower electricity bills by 2040, and would leave emissions flat even under a worst-case fossil-fuel-favorable scenario.

stories.headline: Revolution Wind reaches full commercial operation off New England
stories.summary: Canary Media reports that Ørsted's 704-megawatt Revolution Wind offshore project is now fully operational despite repeated Trump administration stop-work attempts, and will supply power to three Northeast utilities. Utility Dive separately covered the milestone through Eversource's earnings call, noting it reduces the utility's financial risk on the project.

stories.headline: Anthropic strikes $3.4bn gas-fired power deal for data centers
stories.summary: The FT reports that AI lab Anthropic has signed a $3.4 billion deal to generate gas-fired power for data centers, bypassing traditional suppliers to lock up scarce equipment amid surging AI power demand.

stories.headline: COP31 opens in Turkey seeking global electrification pledge
stories.summary: Bloomberg reports that COP31 organizers in Antalya are pushing for a voluntary commitment to raise electricity's share of final global energy demand to 35% by 2035, up from about 20% today, with the summit opening November 9. NYT separately examines how oil-price shocks from the Iran war are simultaneously accelerating EV demand and a scramble for secure fossil-fuel power ahead of the summit.

stories.headline: Berkshire-owned Pacific Power seeks historic 57% California rate hike
stories.summary: WSJ reports that Pacific Power is asking California regulators to approve a 57% rate increase that would raise the typical residential bill by about $120 a month.

stories.headline: DTE Energy sells Vantage subsidiary for $3B, expands investment plan 30%
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports DTE Energy has agreed to sell its non-utility Vantage subsidiary for $3 billion to sharpen its focus on its regulated electric utility, while expanding its five-year investment plan to $44.2 billion including major solar, wind and storage additions.

stories.headline: Trump's foreign grid-component ban sparks industry pushback
stories.summary: Utility Dive reports that Trump's executive order restricting foreign-made grid equipment, intended to protect the bulk power system from security threats, is drawing industry concern that geography-based restrictions could raise costs and slow grid buildout.

Energy.gaps: No recent (last 48h) items could be found for Latitude Media, Carbon Brief, or Argus Media via search. E&E News search results returned mostly older archived pieces, several explicitly noting its energy/environment coverage has moved to Politico Pro, so no clearly current E&E stories were found. Reuters, FT, WSJ, NYT, and The Economist block search, so coverage of those outlets is limited to the feed items provided.

China.description: China politics, economy and business coverage.
China.overview: Coverage this weekend centers on the run-up to the APEC summit in Shenzhen (Nov 18-19), where US and Chinese trade officials held tense talks and Trump and Xi are set to meet, alongside fresh Taiwan-China friction after Taipei closed its Papua New Guinea office. Business and state outlets are also tracking Chinese corporate debt stress, a new anti-corruption law targeting officials who flee overseas, and continued legal fallout from Hong Kong activist Joshua Wong's sentencing.

stories.headline: US and China trade chiefs clash over commitments ahead of Trump-Xi summit in Shenzhen
stories.summary: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and USTR Jamieson Greer held a call with Vice Premier He Lifeng, with Washington stressing the importance of China fully and immediately implementing its commitments and flagging concerns about recent Chinese actions, while Beijing voiced serious concerns over new US trade restrictions, ahead of a planned Xi-Trump meeting at the Shenzhen APEC summit on November 18-19.

stories.headline: Taiwan closes its representative office in Papua New Guinea, blames Chinese coercion
stories.summary: Taiwan said it has decided to close its representative office in Papua New Guinea and withdraw its staff, blaming Chinese coercion of the South Pacific nation for the decision; Nikkei notes the mission had stayed open since PNG first announced plans to shutter it in July.

stories.headline: China's legislature adopts law to hunt down corrupt officials who flee overseas
stories.summary: China's top legislature, the NPC Standing Committee, adopted a new law on cross-border corruption that state-run Global Times called a governance milestone, providing legal support for pursuing corrupt officials and asset-strippers who have fled abroad; Nikkei Asia separately reported the law aims to prevent civil servants and state-owned company bosses from fleeing with assets.

stories.headline: Zhuhai plans land buyback to prop up debt-strained state conglomerate Huafa
stories.summary: A proposed 181 million yuan purchase of an idle hotel site by the Zhuhai municipal government is part of a broader effort to ease funding pressure on Huafa, the city's largest state-owned conglomerate, as it grapples with property losses and heavy debt.

stories.headline: Astellas employee jailed in China on spying charge set for December release
stories.summary: A Japanese national employed by drugmaker Astellas who was jailed in China on espionage charges after reportedly taking a plea deal is set to be released in December, under a law China enacted in 2023 that broadened the range of activities subject to investigation.

stories.headline: SMEE Displays a Dry Lithography Platform Model at CIIE
stories.summary: SMEE showed a cutaway model for a shared i-line/KrF lithography platform and cited over 10 million wafers processed by equipment already on production lines.

China.gaps: No recent China-specific coverage found via search for Sixth Tone, China Media Project, Rest of World, Yicai Global, TechNode, Focus Taiwan, CGTN, The Wire China or direct Xinhua articles; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, WSJ and The Economist block search and had no relevant feed items provided.

Gulf & Middle East.overview: Coverage across Gulf and Middle East outlets is dominated by escalating Yemen-Saudi hostilities after a Houthi strike damaged Riyadh's Aramco tower, and by Israel's political transition as Gadi Eisenkot was handed the mandate to try to form a government over Benjamin Netanyahu. Iran-US tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, Trump's weighing of renewed strikes on Iran, and the deadly Egypt train crash are also drawing heavy cross-outlet attention, alongside a steady stream of UAE economic data.

stories.headline: Houthi missiles damage Saudi Aramco tower in Riyadh financial district
stories.summary: An administrative building belonging to Saudi Aramco in Riyadh's King Abdullah Financial District was damaged by falling debris after the Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted two Houthi ballistic missiles, with no injuries reported. Analysts warned the strike on the financial hub marks a major escalation and a direct hit on the credibility of Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030 economic transformation.

stories.headline: Eisenkot formally tasked with forming Israel's next government, bypassing Netanyahu
stories.summary: Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot formally received the mandate from President Isaac Herzog to try to form Israel's next government after securing 67 recommendations to Netanyahu's 46, despite Likud remaining the single largest party. Eisenkot now has 28 days (with a possible 14-day extension) to assemble a coalition amid deep divisions over the role of Arab and ultra-Orthodox parties.

stories.headline: Trump weighs renewed Iran strikes as advisers clash over war decision
stories.summary: Vice President JD Vance and Gulf allies are reportedly urging Trump to wind down the Iran war, while other advisers push for renewed attacks, as Trump separately told CNN a return to war is "highly unlikely" if talks progress. The debate comes amid reports Washington has cut off some Israel aid and as Mossad and the IDF clash again over Iran strategy.

stories.headline: Iran reports multiple tanker fires and blasts in Strait of Hormuz amid US blockade
stories.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guard said three more tankers exploded and caught fire after striking mines in the Strait of Hormuz, where Tehran has restricted traffic since the war began in February and the US has imposed a naval blockade. Iranian media separately suggested weekend blasts on Qeshm Island and at Jask port were tied to Iranian military activity rather than US strikes, even as both sides reported ships hit.

stories.headline: Egypt train collision south of Cairo kills at least seven, injures over 100
stories.summary: Two passenger trains collided roughly 76 km south of Cairo, killing at least seven people and injuring more than 110, according to Egypt's health ministry, with several carriages derailed. The crash drew condolences and condemnation from regional governments covered across multiple outlets.

stories.headline: Sudan detains Bashir-era official Ahmed Haroun, wanted by ICC
stories.summary: Sudan's army detained Ahmed Haroun, a senior Islamist official from ousted strongman Omar al-Bashir's era who is wanted by the International Criminal Court, officials said.

stories.headline: UAE's nine-month trade nears Dh3 trillion despite regional headwinds
stories.summary: Dubai ruler Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid said the UAE's foreign trade over the first nine months of the year has approached Dh3 trillion, underscoring continued growth despite regional conflict-related disruption.

stories.headline: UAE businesses raise prices at record pace as war-driven costs bite
stories.summary: A closely watched S&P Global survey found UAE companies raised selling prices at the fastest pace since 2009 in October, passing on higher fuel, freight and input costs even as the headline PMI held at 54.8 and firms stayed broadly optimistic. The report flagged this as an early sign of inflation nine months into the Iran war.

Gulf & Middle East.gaps: No distinct recent coverage was found via search for Iran International, Al Arabiya English, Zawya, Saudi Gazette or Haaretz; Reuters, AP, FT, NYT, The Economist and BBC coverage is based only on the feed items provided since these outlets block search.

Africa.description: Africa politics, economy and business coverage.
Africa.overview: Coverage is dominated by South Africa's historic local-election setback for the ANC and the fallout from Washington's decision to strip South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade preferences, alongside a cluster of economic stories on African banking, mining investment and Ethiopia's fragile growth story. Security and political transition stories from Egypt, Nigeria, Gambia and the Horn of Africa round out a newsfeed that spans politics, trade diplomacy and business across the continent.

stories.headline: ANC suffers worst-ever result in South Africa's local elections
stories.summary: Final results confirmed the African National Congress won the most votes in South Africa's local elections but posted its weakest performance since taking power at the end of apartheid, with African Business reporting the party was on track for its worst municipal result ever with 90% of ballots counted.

stories.headline: US strips South Africa and Rwanda of AGOA trade benefits
stories.summary: Washington has removed South Africa and Rwanda from the African Growth and Opportunity Act, making both countries ineligible for tariff-free US trade from January 2027, with US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer citing concerns ranging from South African "corruption" to Rwandan support for the M23 rebel group in Congo. South Africa's trade minister said the country remains open to a solution while a Stellenbosch economist argued the practical cost may be smaller than headlines suggest since much of AGOA's benefit had already been eroded by prior Trump-era tariffs.

stories.headline: Madagascar seeks $5bn with Gemcorp for energy and mining projects
stories.summary: Madagascar is partnering with asset manager Gemcorp Capital Management in a bid to raise as much as $5 billion to fund energy, infrastructure and mining projects in the island nation, according to a Bloomberg report carried by Mining Weekly.

stories.headline: Kenya's biggest banks keep posting record profits as small businesses struggle for credit
stories.summary: TechCabal examines why Kenya's largest lenders continue reporting record profits even as small and medium businesses find it increasingly hard to access affordable credit, pointing to risk aversion and the mechanics of mobile lending.

stories.headline: Ethiopia's economy heats up as security risks mount
stories.summary: Africa Confidential's latest issue reports that positive investment momentum and ambitious economic plans under Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed's government are increasingly threatened by escalating security risks and renewed conflict in the north of the country.

stories.headline: Four dead after two trains collide south of Cairo
stories.summary: Egyptian authorities said four people died and dozens were injured when a train traveling from Fayoum to Giza crashed into another train south of Cairo on Sunday.

stories.headline: Tinubu's son builds Igbo political network to challenge Peter Obi's base ahead of 2027
stories.summary: The Africa Report details how President Tinubu's son Seyi has recruited wealthy Igbo businessmen and former opposition figures to expand his City Boy Movement in Nigeria's southeast, a traditional Peter Obi stronghold, ahead of the 2027 election.

stories.headline: Egypt reopens embassy in Libya to rebuild energy ties with Tripoli
stories.summary: Egypt's foreign minister reopened the country's long-shuttered embassy in Tripoli, a mission that had been closed since 2012, as Cairo seeks to rebuild diplomatic and energy ties with Libya.

Africa.gaps: The Continent could not be searched directly (site returned only general/archival content, nothing dated in the last 48 hours); no current items found. Reuters, AP, BBC, FT and NYT block web search and had no relevant items in the provided feed, so they are not represented beyond what WSJ's feed happened to include.

Media.overview: Media-industry coverage over the past two days clusters around three threads: the escalating standoff between news publishers and AI/tech platforms (Meta's scraping terms, new lawsuits against Brave and Anthropic, and a possible NYT-Letterboxd acquisition), fallout at legacy TV news organizations (CBS's '60 Minutes' blame game, Piers Morgan's lossmaking venture), and a culture-and-politics-infused 'SNL' episode that became a cross-outlet entertainment story following the midterms.

stories.headline: Meta's new AI scraping terms spark publisher backlash and regulatory scrutiny
stories.summary: The UK's News Media Association is urging the government to back the Competition and Markets Authority against Meta's new AI scraping terms, with Norwegian publishers having already won an initial court victory and the CMA opening its own probe; publishers have until November 20 to decide whether to leave Meta's platforms.

stories.headline: Publisher-vs-AI legal war widens: US papers sue Brave, Canadians sue Anthropic
stories.summary: A fresh wave of litigation has hit AI companies, with The New York Times, Chicago Tribune, Daily News and Orlando Sentinel suing browser maker Brave Software over alleged content scraping, while a coalition of Canadian publishers including Torstar and The Globe and Mail is suing Anthropic; meanwhile Reach and CNN have struck new licensing deals with Google.

stories.headline: New York Times reportedly in advanced talks to acquire Letterboxd for $330 million
stories.summary: Nieman Lab's media roundup flagged reporting that New York Times Company is in advanced talks to acquire the film-social-networking app Letterboxd for roughly $330 million, a potential expansion of the Times' subscription and culture-media footprint.

stories.headline: Status: CBS staffers say network brass threw '60 Minutes' journalists under the bus
stories.summary: Oliver Darcy's Status reports that the Trump administration's attack on a '60 Minutes' segment has triggered internal finger-pointing at CBS News, with staffers accusing network leadership of failing to defend its journalists.

stories.headline: 'SNL' turns midterms episode into a viral political-media moment
stories.summary: Saturday Night Live's post-midterms episode, hosted by Druski, drew heavy cross-outlet coverage for Texas senator-elect James Talarico crashing the cold open, a biting Weekend Update parody of Elon Musk over Republicans' election losses, and a whiteface Elizabeth Holmes sketch that drew its own backlash.

stories.headline: Piers Morgan's production company posts £3m loss after leaving News UK
stories.summary: Piers Morgan Uncensored's production company recorded a pre-tax loss of £3m in 2025, a steep reversal from a £7m profit the previous year, even as the operation maintains ambitions to become a top-five digital newsbrand.

stories.headline: 'Godzilla Minus Zero' sets box office records in GKids and global debut
stories.summary: Takashi Yamazaki's sequel opened to roughly $31 million domestically and $63 million worldwide, setting a GKids distribution record and topping Hindu-epic rival 'Ramayana' at the global box office.

Media.gaps: Puck and Columbia Journalism Review had no distinct current (last 48-hour) story found beyond being referenced by rival outlets; NYT, WSJ, FT and The Guardian block direct search and their supplied feed items did not include media-industry-relevant stories.
